title: Adjunction for a monoidal change of enrichment
statement: Let $\mathcal V,\mathcal W$ be presentably monoidal infinity categories and let $f:\mathcal V\to\mathcal W$ be colimit-preserving and strong monoidal, with right adjoint $g$ carrying its adjoint lax monoidal structure. Use [def-coef-complete-algebroid]. Applying $f$ and $g$ to mapping objects gives an adjunction $f_*:\operatorname{Algd}(\mathcal V)\rightleftarrows\operatorname{Algd}(\mathcal W):g_*$. The functor $g_*$ preserves complete objects, and completion on the left gives an adjunction $Lf_*:\operatorname{Cat}_{\mathcal V}\rightleftarrows\operatorname{Cat}_{\mathcal W}:g_*$. The category $\operatorname{Cat}_{\mathrm{Spc}}$ for cartesian-monoidal spaces is equivalent to the infinity category of small infinity categories via the complete Segal-space nerve. Under this equivalence the space-valued mapping objects are the usual mapping spaces. These identifications are natural in coherent diagrams.

source.place: Lemma 4.3.19, Proposition 5.7.17 and Theorem 5.4.6 Read online where available; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical result.

proof.text: Postcomposition defines f_* and g_* on algebroids and on coherent maps, with the same object spaces. To prove they are adjoint, let A have object space X and B have object space Y. Both mapping spaces Map(f_*A,B) and Map(A,g_*B) map to Map_Spc(X,Y). Over phi:X→Y their fibers are respectively Map_{Alg_X(W)}(f_*A,phi^*B) and Map_{Alg_X(V)}(A,g_*(phi^*B)), by the homotopy-fiber formula of lem-coef-algebroid-object-space-fibration. This formula applies to arbitrary monoidal coefficients and arbitrary small X,Y. Replace Delta_X^op by the ordinary operad q(X)=L_gen Delta_X^op using the restriction equivalences of lem-coef-many-object-operad-accessibility. Apply lem-coef-operadic-change-enrichment to q(X). This gives the required equivalence of those fibers, natural in X and phi; g_*phi^*B=phi^*g_*B is the postcomposition/precomposition identity. Its forward map is k↦g_*k∘eta_A, with inverse h↦epsilon_B∘f_*h; these transformations are algebra transformations by that same operadic lemma, and preserve phi. Thus they give maps over the identity of Map_Spc(X,Y), with equivalences on every homotopy fiber. The homotopy-fiber detection lemma makes them equivalences of total mapping spaces. Naturality in A,B follows from the restriction-natural units and counits, and the pointwise adjoint criterion supplies the coherent adjunction f_*⊣g_*.

Strong monoidality gives f_*E^n≃E^n coherently in maps between the finite object sets: every mapping object is the tensor unit and f carries its unit constraints to those of W. In particular f_* sends s:E^1→E^0 to the same s. For complete B, the locality characterization and step 1 identify Map(E^0,g_*B)→Map(E^1,g_*B) with Map(E^0,B)→Map(E^1,B); the latter is an equivalence. Hence g_*B is s-local and therefore complete. This proves the required preservation without imposing any condition on the object space of B.

Algd(V) and Algd(W) are presentable by lem-coef-algebroid-presentability. The singleton {s} is small in the fixed universes, and lem-coef-algebroid-completion identifies its local objects with Cat_V and Cat_W. Apply the small-localization clause of lem-coef-presentable-infinity-adjoints to obtain reflectors L_V and L_W. For complete C,D, step 2 and fullness give the natural chain Map_Cat_W(L_W f_*C,D)≃Map_Algd(W)(f_*C,D)≃Map_Algd(V)(C,g_*D)≃Map_Cat_V(C,g_*D). The middle equivalence is step 1 and the first is the reflector adjunction. The mapping-space criterion gives L_W f_*⊣g_* on complete objects, with coherent units, counits and triangle identities.

Let $T$ be the terminal monoidal infinity category (one object $*$, only identities, $T^\otimes=\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$) and take $S=\varnothing$ in [lem-coef-algebroid-segal-localization-model]. Evaluation at $*$ identifies $P(T)$ with $\mathrm{Spc}$. Monoidal identification: the unit functor $u:T\to\mathrm{Spc}$, $*\mapsto*$, is strong monoidal for the cartesian structure, its enhancement being the section of $\mathrm{Spc}^\times\to\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ through the unit tuples $(*,\ldots,*)$; cocartesian transport sends a unit tuple to the tuple of block products of points, again a unit tuple, so every arrow goes to a cocartesian arrow. By the last clause of [lem-coef-operadic-day-convolution] (spaces are cocomplete and cartesian product preserves colimits separately), the colimit-preserving Yoneda extension $u_!:P(T)\to\mathrm{Spc}$ is strong monoidal for Day convolution. It preserves colimits and sends $y(*)=*$ to $*$, so under evaluation it is the identity of $\mathrm{Spc}$. Hence $P(T)$ with Day convolution is monoidally equivalent to cartesian-monoidal spaces, and postcomposition gives $\operatorname{Algd}(P(T))\simeq\operatorname{Algd}(\mathrm{Spc})$. The cartesian fibration $T_\otimes\to\Delta$ is classified by the constant functor at a point, so $T_\otimes\simeq\Delta$, every list $\boldsymbol c$ is $(*,\ldots,*)$, and $P(T_\otimes)$ is simplicial spaces. The Segal condition of [def-coef-segal-presheaf-localization] then reads $Z_n\simeq Z_1\times_{Z_0}\cdots\times_{Z_0}Z_1$, so $Q_T$ is the Segal spaces of [lem-coef-complete-segal-quasicategory-comparison]. The model equivalence gives $N:\operatorname{Algd}(\mathrm{Spc})\simeq\mathrm{Seg}_\infty$, identifying $X_A$ with $Z_0$ and $A(x,y)$ with the arrow fibre $H_Z(x,y)(*)$ of $Z=N(A)$, compatibly with the canonical unit and composition maps. For $\phi=*$ one has $a_\phi=*$ and $E_T(*)=\Delta^1$, so the model's displayed formula gives $Z_1\simeq\int_{(x,y)\in Z_0^2}H_Z(x,y)(*)$ over $Z_0^2$.

With $N$, $Z=N(A)$ and the arrow-fibre formula of step 4: $E^1$ has object set $\{0,1\}$ and all mapping objects $*$, so by the same formula the point of the arrow fibre of $N(E^1)$ at $(0,1)$ is a map $\Delta^1\to N(E^1)$ with endpoints $0,1$. Restriction along it gives $w:I_1(A)=\operatorname{Map}(E^1,A)\simeq\operatorname{Map}(N(E^1),Z)\to\operatorname{Map}(\Delta^1,Z)=Z_1$ over $X_A^2=Z_0^2$. On the fibre over $(x,y)$ it is evaluation of $E^1\to A$ on the arrow $*=E^1(0,1)\to A(x,y)$, followed by $A(x,y)\simeq H_Z(x,y)(*)$. By [lem-coef-algebroid-equivalence-nerve] this evaluation identifies that fibre of $I_1(A)$ with the invertible components of $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathrm{Spc}}(*,A(x,y))=A(x,y)$. Because $N$ respects units and composition, these are exactly the arrows invertible in the homotopy category of $Z$, i.e. the fibre of $Z_{\mathrm{eq}}$. So $w$ lands in $Z_{\mathrm{eq}}$ and is an equivalence on every fibre over the identity of $X_A^2$; [lem-coef-spaces-homotopy-fiber-detection] gives $w:I_1(A)\simeq Z_{\mathrm{eq}}$. Under $w$ and $I_0(A)\simeq X_A=Z_0$, precomposition with $s:E^1\to E^0$ becomes $s_0:Z_0\to Z_{\mathrm{eq}}$, since $s$ sends the arrow of $E^1$ to the identity. By [lem-coef-algebroid-completion], $A$ is complete exactly when $\operatorname{Map}(E^0,A)\to\operatorname{Map}(E^1,A)$ is an equivalence, i.e. exactly when $Z$ is Rezk complete. Restricting $N$ and its inverse to these full subcategories gives $\operatorname{Cat}_{\mathrm{Spc}}\simeq\mathrm{CSS}_\infty$. Composing with $R^{-1}$ from [lem-coef-complete-segal-quasicategory-comparison] gives $\operatorname{Cat}_{\mathrm{Spc}}\simeq\mathrm{Cat}_\infty$.

For complete $A$ put $C=R^{-1}N(A)$ with $N$ from step 4 and $R$ from step 5, and let $e:N(A)\simeq R(C)$ be the counit equivalence. Its components $e_0,e_1$ commute with the endpoint maps $(-)_1\to(-)_0^2$ up to their simplicial homotopies. Applying $e_1$ to an arrow and $e_0$ to its endpoint paths defines a map from the homotopy fibre at $(x,y)$ to the one at $(e_0x,e_0y)$. Since $e_1$ and $e_0\times e_0$ are equivalences, [lem-coef-spaces-homotopy-fiber-detection] makes this fibre map an equivalence. The source fibre is $A(x,y)$ by the identification from [lem-coef-algebroid-segal-localization-model] used in step 4. The target fibre is $\operatorname{Map}_C(e_0x,e_0y)$ by [lem-coef-complete-segal-quasicategory-comparison]. Hence $A(x,y)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_C(e_0x,e_0y)$, naturally in $A$, $x$, $y$, because the model identification, $e$ and the Rezk-node identification are natural.

For any small indexing infinity category K, postcomposition sends a K-diagram U to f_*U or g_*U and sends a transformation to its image. The units and counits of steps 1 and 3 give transformations on these diagrams whose components at k are eta_{U(k)} and epsilon_{U(k)}; their naturality squares and higher simplices are those of the original coherent transformations. For diagrams U,V, the assignments a↦g_*(a)∘eta_U and b↦epsilon_V∘f_*(b) are inverse maps on the diagram mapping spaces: their composites are the identities by naturality and the two triangle homotopies, evaluated on the whole diagrams. Use L_W f_* in place of f_* for the complete-object adjunction. Likewise, postcomposing diagrams with N, R and their chosen inverses gives inverse functors, with the postcomposed unit/counit equivalences. The mapping-fiber identifications of step 6 commute with diagram arrows and higher simplices by their stated naturality. Thus the adjunctions and comparison identifications have the asserted coherent diagram naturality.
